demos.label: 1. iAssist
demos.description: Internal iAssist platform workflow with prior authorization approval

demos.label: 2. iAssist Appeal
demos.description: Structural clone of iAssist (WF4), but the PA is denied instead of approved, sets up the Action Factory appeal-rule demo

demos.label: 3. iAssist Medical Transfer
demos.description: The medical benefit covers it and a PA is required. HCP administered (Buy & Bill): the Rx transfers to an assigned pharmacy with no payment or scheduling

demos.label: 4. iAssist Buy and Bill
demos.description: The HCP buys and bills under the medical benefit. eMedBV, a medical PA, and HCP-enrolled copay, with a copay claim after approval. No pharmacy, payment, or delivery. The patient consents by text and confirms household income in the patient app

demos.label: 5. iAssist Buy and Bill, HCP captures consent
demos.description: The same Buy and Bill story, but the HCP captures consent and household income on the iAssist form, so the patient app asks for neither

demos.label: 6. iAssist Buy and Bill, Free Drug
demos.description: eMedBV finds no medical coverage, so there is no PA or copay. The patient applies for the free drug program, and approval sends the drug to the site of care. The patient pays nothing
